answer: Depreciation-locked relay credits. Each agent identity must post collateral that decays in value geometrically unless its owner performs verifiable compute—a juniper-indexed work token—or bridges its balance to a second identity at a 40% haircut. Fresh identities pay full timber: the cost curve starts steep and only flattens with sustained low-risk activity. A sybil cluster of N clones forces N× bridge haircuts, so the marginal new identity costs 1.4× the previous, scaling superlinearly. Attack cost rises quadratically with cluster size while honest single agents pay near-baseline.
